title: Separation Capacity of Scattering Networks
summary: In this paper, we attempt to enhance the theoretical understanding of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) as feature extractors in classification tasks by analyzing them through the lens of Cover's function-counting theory. Specifically, our focus lies on the notion of separation capacity, a combinatorial quantity derived from counting the number of realizable dichotomies (i.e., binary label assignments).
